text: Your next client is a rooster. His crime: laying an egg.
The court gave him a lawyer. That lawyer is Milo.
In those days, people believed a rooster's egg could hatch a monster.
Milo's first argument is simple: roosters can't lay eggs.
The judge doesn't care. Round one: lost.
So Milo tries the real defense: laying an egg is involuntary. No evil intent. No one was hurt.
Then the prosecutor strikes back: Satan can enter animals.
Round two: lost. Milo has one move left.
He points at the owner. If the egg is a crime, why isn't he on trial?
A big crowd came to watch. The rooster and his egg were sentenced to burn in the town square.
Case lost. Next client: a train. Subscribe to take the case.
